The shoebox under her bed says "DON'T TELL MOM." 📦 Stop doing these, if you don't want her to fill it.

Kids don't stop making mistakes. They stop telling you, because they're afraid of how you'll react. Mia, year by year:
✅ Don't punish the truth. "I broke it." "GROUNDED!"
✅ Not every mistake needs a lecture.
✅ Don't call her "too sensitive."
✅ Don't compare her. "Your cousin got an A!"
✅ What's small to you is huge to her. Not "that's nothing."
✅ No disappointed sigh.
✅ Make "I made a mistake" less scary than "What did you DO?!"

By fourteen, the box is full. 😔

In a study of 372 kids aged 4-8, hearing "the truth makes me happy" made children far more honest than the threat of punishment.

So Mom changes her first words. Spilled juice? "Thanks for telling me." ❤️ And one night, when Mia faces something she can't fix alone, she brings it straight to Mom. "I'm so glad you told me." 🥹

That's how God treats us. "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness." 1 John 1:9 (ESV) 🙏 Jesus paid for it in full, so we never have to hide.

Be the one they run to. ❤️ Worries too.
